title: Prefill lazy-heuristic throttler: reduce per-request prefill overhead for short prompts
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Problem: Short user prompts (<= 64 chars) account for ~42% of RPS on hosted tier but still incur prefill-side canonicalization/normalization and tokenization paths that add 0.9–1.4ms p50 per request. This overhead becomes material for low-latency tiers and for small decode budgets. Existing prefill code path runs full unicode normalization, expensive session lookup, and a memory-copy heavy token buffer allocation even when the prompt is trivial.

Proposal: Implement a "lazy-heuristic throttler" on the prefill ingest path that performs a cheap early-exit check and routes the request to one of three lanes:
- Fast accept lane: ascii-only, short length, no session prefix -> run lightweight tokenizer variant (byte-level fast path), skip KV cache lookup, allocate from thread-local pool.
- Hybrid cached lane: medium-length prompts or requests with known session prefixes -> consult small per-worker LRU of recent tokenization results (hybrid locality cache) and run canonical tokenizer with zero-copy when cache hit.
- Full normalization lane: long or complex unicode inputs, or requests with transforms -> fallback to existing path.

Key enhancements:
- Early-exit heuristics: ascii-only predicate + punctuation ratio + small length -> O(1) checks using vectorized 64-bit masks.
- Per-worker microcache: bounded LRU (128 entries) keyed by 64-bit content fingerprint + model-id + session-seed; store compact token slices and precomputed kernel-hints for the decoder.
- Kernel hint propagation: when cache hit, attach small metadata (quantized sequence length bucket, attention-sparsity hint) to the request so scheduler can pick optimized kernels and attention gating variants.
- Microbatch-aware throttling: if short prompts are surging, coalesce their prefill ingestion into a dedicated microbatch queue with priority on throughput (to avoid head-of-line blocking for longer decodes).

Benefits expected:
- Reduce median prefill CPU time for short prompts by ~0.7ms and p95 by ~1.1ms in our internal small-model benchmarks.
- Increase overall throughput for high-concurrency small prompt workloads by ~18% due to reduced per-request alloc/free churn and better batching compatibility.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Prototype ASCII-only fast accept lane in userland tokenizer module + thread-local allocator (spike + microbench) (owner: Marco) (2d).
2) Implement per-worker microcache with eviction metrics and instrumentation + content fingerprinting (owner: Aisha) (3d).
3) Kernel-hint metadata struct (compact bytes) + scheduler hook to prefer specialized kernels when present (owner: Kernel team lead) (4d). Dependency: ENG-100207 for kernel hint API.
4) Microbatch coalescer: queue implementation and fairness policy, integrate with existing batching router (owner: SRE/Batching) (3d). Dependency: ENG-47288 for batching stability fixes.
5) Canary rollout on a small customer segment (10%) with telemetry gating (tokenization hit rate, prefill latency, decode success) and automatic rollback criteria.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fast accept lane active and exercised in production with at least 30% of short prompts hitting it.
- p50 prefill latency for <=64 char prompts reduced by >=0.5ms on hosted API on the runtime-1.20 branch.
- No measurable increase in tokenization correctness regressions; automated fuzz harness (see attachments) passes 100K random unicode inputs.
- Kernel hint metadata is consumed by scheduler and results in measurable selection of optimized kernels for cached requests.

Tests & verification:
- Unit tests for ascii predicate, LRU correctness, and zero-copy buffer semantics.
- End-to-end integration tests calling hosted API emulator with mixed-length workloads.
- Performance microbench suite: run against model-llm-small and model-llm-medium on cpu/gpu nodes to validate numbers.

Rollout & monitoring:
- Dashboard: prefill-lane-breakdown, microcache hitrate, per-lane p50/p95, allocator contention.
- Canary for 72 hours then ramp to 50% if no regressions; automatic rollback on sustained +10% p95 prefill latency or increase in tokenization error rate.

Risks & mitigations:
- False positives in ascii predicate -> ensure fallback to full path and keep correctness tests; maintain conservative predicate until metrics stable.
- Cache poisoning via crafted inputs -> use cryptographic salt per-worker for fingerprinting and ttl-based eviction.
- Scheduler coupling complexity -> keep kernel hint optional (best-effort) and fall back to legacy kernel selection on mismatch.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Prefill+Lazy+Heuristic+Throttler
- Microbench results (raw): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PrefillPerf
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9876

Operational note: this change targets runtime-1.20 and is backward compatible; the microcache data is ephemeral and not persisted across restarts.
